name: Moise Nicoară National College
address: Piața Moise Nicoară 1 (also listed as Piața Margareta Bibici)
hint: Your trail starts at a historic school on a quiet square, near the city’s classic theatre.
description:
Moise Nicoară National College is a public day high school and one of the most prestigious pre-university schools in Arad. It was founded in 1873 as a Catholic high school, and its roots reach back to 1707, when the Bavarian monk Kamill Höfflich set up the first elementary school in the city.

In October 1919, after the union of Transylvania with Romania, the school took its present name, honoring the 19th-century cultural figure and patriot Moise Nicoară, and became the first Romanian-language boys’ high school in Arad. It became a high school again in 1965, readopted the Nicoară name in 1991, and has been a “National College” since the 2000–2001 school year.

The Renaissance-style building was raised between 1869 and 1873 and restored in 2011. It stands in a square close to the Ioan Slavici Classic Theatre. The college is known for its Mathematics-Informatics and Natural Sciences classes and for olympiad results, including a recent silver medal at the International Chemistry Olympiad won by one of its graduates.
